clue.text: Part of Turkey divided by some with secret aspirations?

definitions.text: Part of Turkey divided by some with secret aspirations?

parts.words: Part of Turkey divided by some with secret aspirations?
parts.note: the forked breastbone of a roast bird, pulled apart by two diners who each make a silent wish; the capital T makes it look like the country

explanation.surface: A region of the country of Turkey is carved up by conspirators with hidden ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' with its capital looks like the country, but it is the Christmas bird; the 'secret aspirations' are the wishes made as the bone is pulled.
explanation.definitionFit: The forked bone from a fowl's breast is snapped by two people, the one left with the larger piece supposedly getting their wish.

clue.text: Domestic servant finally replacing folio lost by subordinate

indicators.note: replacing says one letter takes the place of another in the word for subordinate

parts.note: a subordinate is an inferior, someone of lower rank

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word servant

explanation.surface: A household servant ends up taking over after a page is lost by a junior employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost by' is a link: the F of INFERIOR is lost and T, the last letter of 'servant' (signalled by 'finally'), goes in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic affairs are internal or home ones, as in a government's ministry for internal affairs.

clue.text: Large mammal cut down in St Augustine's city

definitions.text: Large mammal cut down in St Augustine's city

parts.words: Large mammal cut down in St Augustine's city
parts.note: shorten the name of the big African river beast and you get the name of the North African town where St Augustine was bishop

explanation.surface: A big animal was slaughtered in the town where St Augustine lived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down' suggests killing, but it means abbreviated: the animal's short name is also Hippo Regius, the Roman city in Algeria where Augustine was bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: The huge African river-dwelling beast's common short name matches Augustine's city of Hippo.

clue.text: Non-member not allowed drink, say

parts.note: out means not permitted, as a ruling of out of bounds

indicators.note: say signals that the drink is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic apple drink

explanation.surface: Someone who is not in the club is refused a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals a sound-alike: the apple drink is heard, not spelt, so its first letter changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not belonging to a group stands beyond its circle, a stranger to it.

clue.text: In which one body may be overshadowed by another

definitions.text: In which one body may be overshadowed by another

parts.words: In which one body may be overshadowed by another
parts.note: the bodies are celestial ones, such as the moon passing in front of the sun and blotting out its light

explanation.surface: A situation where one person is put in the shade by a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body' suggests a person upstaged by another, but it means a heavenly body blocking another's light.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon passes between earth and sun it obscures the sun, a cosmic overshadowing.

clue.text: Gun law, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or spoken, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: a canon is a law or rule, especially of the church

explanation.surface: A firearms statute, as people are saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' tells you to take CANON, a church law, by its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A large heavy artillery piece firing balls is a big gun.

clue.text: Swindler abandons daughter, a German woman

indicators.note: abandons means the swindler's word lets go of a letter, dropping it

parts.note: a fraud is a cheat or swindler

explanation.surface: A con man walks out on his daughter and takes up with a woman from Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' removes the D (daughter) from FRAUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Frau is the German title and word for a married lady, the equivalent of Mrs.

clue.text: Very clean location? Not so

parts.note: a spot is a place or location
less means not so much, to a smaller degree

explanation.surface: A remark about a place that is spotless, followed by a denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so' reads like a contradiction but supplies LESS, to a lesser degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a single mark or stain is immaculate.

clue.text: Cobblers show approval of gin

parts.note: to clap is to applaud, showing approval
a gin is a snare or trap for catching animals

explanation.surface: Shoemakers applaud a glass of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' is British slang for nonsense, not shoemakers; 'gin' is the snare, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobblers is British slang for rubbish talk, empty pretentious nonsense.

clue.text: Possibly the organist's principal port of call

definitions.meaning: the principal is one of the sets of pipes an organist selects with a knob or tab
a place where a journey pauses, a halt on the way

explanation.surface: Perhaps the main harbour an organ player visits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal' looks like an adjective meaning main, but it is the name of an organ register, controlled by a drawknob.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ register such as the principal is selected by a knob of that name, and a halt on a route also goes by it.

clue.text: Enthusiasm appropriate when consuming game and granadilla

parts.note: passion is strong enthusiasm

indicators.note: consuming means the word for appropriate swallows up the game's letters

parts.note: fit means suitable or appropriate
RU stands for rugby union, the game

explanation.surface: Keenness is appropriate when eating game and a tropical fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when consuming' signals a container; the game is rugby union, abbreviated in crosswords by its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The granadilla is a tropical fruit of the passiflora vine, an example of this kind.

clue.text: As a barrister might, carrying heavy luggage?

definitions.meaning: a lawyer ends their argument in court by declaring they have nothing more to add
a weary traveller might set down a heavy bag for a breather

explanation.surface: Like a lawyer, lugging a weighty bag.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is first the courtroom formula for finishing an argument, then read literally as giving a suitcase a breather.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister concludes their argument with this formula; a porter with a heavy bag might literally set it down for a break.

clue.text: Transparent cover split by mischievous child

indicators.note: split by means the cover word is broken open with another word inside

parts.note: a lid is a cover
an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A see-through lid is broken by a naughty youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split by' signals a container: the cover is broken open around the youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid water is clear, so clear you can see through it.

clue.text: Smooth official initially in novel footwear

parts.note: to sand is to smooth with abrasive paper

indicators.note: in tells you the official's first letter goes inside the novel's title

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of official

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking official appears early on in a novel about shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE is H. Rider Haggard's novel; O, the first letter of 'official' (signalled by 'initially'), goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandshoe is a canvas plimsoll, a light shoe for the beach.

clue.text: Small chapel used for public speaking?

definitions.meaning: a small place of private worship
the art of making speeches, the skill of rhetoric

explanation.surface: A little church that hosts lectures.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a private chapel and the art of eloquent public address.

clue.text: Proscription involving western king in expenditure

indicators.note: involving means the expenditure word contains the other letters

parts.note: an outlay is an expenditure
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A ban that drags in a cowboy king's spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts W (western) and R (rex, king) inside OUTLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Proscription is banishing someone from the law's protection, declaring them a criminal outcast.

clue.text: Exertions directed to having amphibians about

indicators.note: about means the amphibians' word goes round the other

parts.note: efts are newts, small amphibians
for means directed to, intended for

explanation.surface: Hard work directed at keeping some newts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals a container: the newts surround the preposition; 'having' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Efforts are attempts involving hard work, strenuous endeavours.

clue.text: Lie about runs gives rise to animosity

indicators.note: about means the lie's word goes around the runs letter

parts.note: fiction is an invented story, a lie
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Lying about runs scored causes bad feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R (runs, a cricket abbreviation) inside FICTION; 'gives rise to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction between people is conflict and hostility, a figurative rubbing.

clue.text: Current keeping river extremely warm

indicators.note: keeping means the current word holds the river letter inside it

parts.note: topical means current, of present interest

explanation.surface: An ocean current holding a river very warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like a flow of water but means up-to-date, TOPICAL, which keeps R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical weather is hot and humid, like that near the equator.

clue.text: Young actress created scare, delaying opening of theatre

indicators.note: delaying means a letter is moved later in the word, held back to the end

parts.note: to startle is to create a scare or fright

indicators.note: opening of picks the first letter of theatre

explanation.surface: A young actress caused alarm by holding up the start of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delaying' moves a T, the 'opening of theatre', from the middle of STARTLE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A starlet is a young, ambitious film actress hoping for stardom.

clue.text: Bull only tethered at first beside private river

parts.note: Tommy is a nickname for a private British soldier

indicators.note: at first picks the first letter of each of the words only and tethered

explanation.surface: A bull, alone and tied up at first, next to a soldier by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bull' is slang for nonsense, not the animal. TOMMY is the British nickname for a private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Bull is slang for drivel, as is this old British word for nonsense.

clue.text: Soak up port before being involved in disturbance

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the soak word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp

explanation.surface: Drink up in port before getting caught up in a fracas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' in a down clue signals a reversal; to ret is to soak flax so its fibres loosen, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A being here is a creature or person: one who takes part in an unruly public uproar.

clue.text: Where food is preserved in current church buffet?

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
CE is the Church of England
to buffet is to box, strike

explanation.surface: Where food is kept at a church's buffet meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' suggests a meal but is the verb, to strike, giving BOX.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is a cold cabinet keeping provisions chilled, an old word for a fridge.

clue.text: Patrician trait Corsica developed

indicators.note: developed means the letters are worked up into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noble quality was developed in Corsica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges TRAIT and CORSICA together.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrician means belonging to the nobility, the upper class of Rome and beyond.

clue.text: Armed warriors in the 2 of 13

indicators.note: the 2 refers to the answer to 2 down, the inside, so it means the inner letters of the word

parts.note: the answer to 13 across is a word for transparent

explanation.surface: Fighters inside a numbered cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 down's answer is the inside part; 13 across gives LIMPID, whose interior, without its first and last letters, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment of warriors.

clue.text: Painter going over church gateway

indicators.note: going over means the painter's letters turn round, flipping backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: An artist visits a church entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' signals a reversal of the Royal Academician, a crossword stock painter.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch is a curved structure over an opening, as in a ceremonial entrance.

clue.text: Power state invested in magistrate to give pardon

indicators.note: invested in means placed within the magistrate's word

parts.note: a reeve was an old local magistrate
RI is Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: Authority is vested in a magistrate so a pardon can be granted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' signals a container; a reeve was a medieval English local official, and the state is Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprieve is to cancel or postpone a punishment, granting clemency.

clue.text: Offer half only, in affectionate manner

parts.note: to tender is to offer

indicators.note: half takes the second two letters of only

explanation.surface: Proposing only half, but doing so lovingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the back half of the clue word 'only'; the front half would not fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderly means gently and lovingly, with kindness.
